title: Investigate & fix ARP/MAC-table collapse on Dedicated hosts during GPU pool drain causing transient tenant reachability and resolver misbind
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During scheduled GPU pool drain operations (scale-down / host evacuation) on Dedicated clusters we observed transient loss of tenant isolation and intermittent DNS/resolver misbinding for a subset of tenants. Some requests from tenant A were being routed to tenant B's resolver instance for a 30-90s window after host failover, causing failed internal hostname resolutions and request routing errors.

Context:
This started as Tier-1 customer escalations from two Dedicated customers running heavy inference workloads in NYC region (Acme Health, TruBank). They reported sporadic 5xxs and incorrect hostname resolutions during predictable maintenance windows. Initial triage indicated no control-plane misconfiguration and no policy changes at the time of errors.

Why this ticket:
We need a durable fix that prevents MAC/ARP collapse and resolver binding bleed during host drain and VNI reassignments, add compensating reconciliation logic, and harden observability and mitigations.
reproduction_steps:
1) Provision a dedicated GPU pool and create two tenants sharing the same VNI range.
2) Start sustained inference traffic from both tenants with frequent short-lived connections and large ephemeral port churn.
3) Trigger host drain (kubectl cordon/drain equivalent for inference host) causing container tasks to be rescheduled across hosts and VNIs to be rebalanced.
4) Observe that within ~10-90s after drain completion some source IPs get associated to incorrect resolver instances; DNS lookups for tenant-internal hostnames fail or resolve to other tenant IPs.
5) Check overlay agent MAC table and ARP cache on the evacuated host and the target host — entries are stale or collapsed and not reconciled until a delayed sweep runs.

Remarks: This is non-deterministic but reliably reproduces under load and fast host churn; we reproduced in staging with a deterministic host-drain script.
mitigation:
Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back a recent autoscaler change that increased concurrent drain parallelism.
- Added a conservative 15s post-drain quiesce delay before marking VNI reassignment complete.
- Forced a manual overlay-agent MAC/ARP sweep and resolver binding reconciliation for affected clusters (runbook step).
- Temporarily limited ephemeral SNAT port reuse per-tenant to reduce cross-tenant port reassociation.
These reduced customer reports during the maintenance window but are not acceptable long-term due to cost and latency impact.

root_cause:
Combination of factors produced a race that caused transient tenant isolation failures: (1) Host drain triggers rapid container rescheduling and VNI reallocation while overlay agents were concurrently tearing down and rebuilding L2 learning tables. (2) The overlay agent's teardown path collapsed MAC entries without enqueuing a reconciliation marker for the destination host; consequently, the destination host briefly accepted traffic with leftover resolver bindings attributed to the old host. (3) Ephemeral SNAT port reuse logic allowed quick reallocation of ports between tenants; when resolver binding moved during the same window, packets were associated with the wrong resolver.

In short: asynchronous VNI/MAC teardown + delayed reconciliation + aggressive SNAT port reuse = transient resolver misbind and cross-tenant reachability leakage.
fix_description:
Permanent fix (implemented behind feature flag PR 4337):
- overlay-agent: on host-drain, explicit tombstone entries are created for MAC/ARP keys and a reconciliation marker is published to the control plane. The destination agent will perform an immediate soft-sweep for keys tagged with recent tombstones.
- control-plane: ensure VNI reassignment completes only after reconciliation acknowledgement (opt-in per-cluster to avoid slowdowns for non-dedicated pools).
- snat-manager: introduce tenant-aware ephemeral-port allocation buckets and a short cooldown before reusing ephemeral ports across tenant scopes.
- add metrics: mac_tombstones_created, mac_reconcile_latency, resolver_binding_mismatch_count and alert thresholds.

Code references and discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4337, design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/NET/ARP+Tombstone+and+Reconcile+Design
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable feature-flag on 10 staging hosts and run host-drain stress for 48h; monitor mac_reconcile_latency and resolver_binding_mismatch_count.
Phase 2 (prod-limited): enable on 8 production hosts in nyc that host low-criticality tenants; 24h watch with automatic rollback if mismatch_count > 0 for 5m.
Phase 3 (prod-wide): enable for all Dedicated hosts in nyc after 72h cool period with metrics stable; then roll through eu region.
Abort criteria: any sustained increase in p99 latency for control-plane route reconciles, increase in resolver_binding_mismatch_count, or unexplained 5xx spike in tenant traffic.
Post-rollout: run a cluster-wide sweep script to remove stale MAC entries older than 2m and record reconciliation success metrics.
